newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan govt seeks early conclusion of NTT break-up.
newsitem.headline: Japan govt seeks early conclusion of NTT break-up.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications hopes to reach agreement with Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp as soon as possible on a plan to break-up the firm, a ministry official said on Monday.
The official, however, denied a newspaper report which said that the ministry and the firm had reached an agreement to break up the firm as early as 1998/99 business year.
A spokesman for Nippon Telegraph and Telephone (NTT) also said that there has been no agreement on the proposed break up.

The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said that the ministry plans to submit a bill to revise a law limiting NTT to domestic services during a regular parliamentary session to be convened in January, paving the way for NTT to get an international long-distance licence.
The ministry has long said that NTT, which has a monopoly over Japan's local networks, cannot be allowed an international licence unless it is broken up into smaller companies.
